back: l(t) = alpha*y(t) + (1-alpha)*l(t-1). The forecast for all future steps is the last level.
How fast the level reacts. Alpha near 1 follows the newest value. Alpha near 0 changes slowly.
The naive forecast: the level equals the last observed value.

front: What is the weight of the value k steps back?
back: alpha times (1 - alpha) to the power k. The weights decay exponentially.
Minimise the sum of squared one-step errors on training data only. Use a grid or an optimiser.

front: Why does SES fail on trending data?
back: Its forecast is flat. A rising series stays above it, so the errors are always positive.
